title: GT17-670GD - EVOLVED OPERATIONAL USER INTERFACES (EXPRO+)
description: Existing operational user interfaces for ground segment are primarily built on aging software platforms characterized by deprecated technologies, a monolithic architecture and rigid implementation. While these legacy platforms provide stability for established scenarios, it struggles to adapt to modern operational demands specifically the introduction of remote operations, cloud infrastructure management, and the seamless integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Building on the EGS-CC WebUI and the PulseUI, a specialized WebUI branch tailored for operational environments, the new approach has enabled support for comprehensive UI testing, facilitate remote control capabilities, and better align with the microservices architecture backends. To overcome these challenges and achieve the goals of the project, an architectural and design approach based on the following will be required: - Web-Based Architecture: To guarantee high flexibility and stability. - Unified Design System: Establishing a common look and feel across the ground segment.  - Industry-Standard Framework Principles: Adopting the principles of established UI frameworks (such as Material Design). This will provide a comprehensive suite of reusable components, complete with intuitive documentation and tutorials, hence mitigates the risk of "technology islands".

title: GT1D-613SY - METHODOLOGY TO UPDATE OPERATIONAL MODELS OF A SPACECRAFT SYSTEM (EXPRO+)
description: Simulation models developed at design, AIT and operations phases shall be recalibrated based on the flight experience. Currently, during operation, the predictive simulations performed by design, AIT and operations teams with simulators are not fully connected toflight telemetry. Therefore, the simulators do not reflect the real state of the spacecraft and the lessons learned are not transferred to the models for the next spacecraft. The activity aims at streamlining the process, enhancing the fidelity and representativeness of the simulation models and reducing the effort for models update and reusability. In this activity, to implement the correction of the model, an assessment to define the origin of the deviation shall be made considering the latest advancement in digitalization, model calibration and synchronization, leveraging the concepts of digital twins' spacecraft. Furthermore, state of the art approaches of surrogate modelling, AI and Machine Learning shall be considered to enhance representativeness and fidelity. The experimentation plan shall be extended in a multidisciplinary way, to improve the method, including in-flight data, and to prepare multidisciplinary optimization to improve operations, future design and reduce the margins.

title: S2P S2-VS-06 VISDOMS-S PHASE A/B1
description: The procurement covers the VISDOMS-S Mission Phase A/B1. Based on the previous Space Based Optical Monitoring (SBOM) feasibility study, a mission concept using a small satellite and existing imager shall be further elaborated in a short Phase A. Suitable small platform candidates shall be further investigated in terms of its capacity and compliance towards the observational needs, the deorbiting requirements, and its capability to host the identified optical imager. The preliminary technical, engineering and quality assurance requirements for the Delta-Class mission shall be reviewed, agreed and consolidated as part of the Preliminary Requirements Review. The development approach shall be further elaborated with the objective to enable the establishment of the implementation and procurement plan. System optimisations based on previous flight experience that may lead to an improvement of the mission performance and its robustness by enhancing the existing equipment and optical imager may be considered for further elaboration during Phase B1.The Phase B1 industrial system study shall produce a preliminary design of the space and ground segment that shall include all elements for the mission definition, the spacecraft and the optical imager and the ground segment. The satellite design shall be matured, and a detailed accommodation study of the optical imager shall be performed. The design of the optical imager and potential modifications that may be required shall be addressed including the detector selection, readout electronics and the control and data processing unit. The technical requirements specifications of all major units shall be established, and the system requirements shall be consolidated and verified as far as possible by analysis. The study shall produce the necessary documentation for the System Requirements Review and confirm that the review objectives are achieved.

title: EARTH ACTION - GDA NEXT GENERATION MAINSTREAMING ELEMENT ON POVERTY-FRAGILITY-DISASTER NEXUS - EXPRO+
description: The activity aims to support the mainstreaming and operational adoption of EO-based solutions for fragility, poverty and disaster-related applications, building on the priorities and operational needs identified through the co-design process with IFIs.Focus willbe given to priority areas such as measuring fragility, damage assessment and service disruption in conflict-affected settings, andother applications supporting decision-making in fragile and crisis contexts.The activity will address the conditions required forsustained uptake, including validation, usability, interoperability with existing user systems and analytical frameworks, scalability,and integration into institutional workflows. It will also assess suitable delivery, governance and business models to enable the continued operational use of the developed indicators, data products and analytical capabilities beyond individual demonstrations.Theoverall objective is to develop and operationalise sustainable EO-enabled capabilities that can be embedded in the operational processes of IFIs.
